goals: Mechanistic: contrast water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage/recharge, snow storage) between a wet year (1993) and a dry year (2002) across the basin's elevation/soil heterogeneity
Validation: compare simulated hydrologic response to in-domain observations (USGS gauges) — collides with no-routing limit

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the full water balance and its partitioning; the wet/dry contrast is a forcing-period treatment applied per column, and NLDAS-2 supplies elevation-varying precip/temperature across the 2400 m relief.

answerable: Wet-year vs dry-year contrast in ET, runoff, drainage and soil-moisture partitioning per column (forcing period is fully supported within 1980-2018)
Elevation-resolved differences in the wet/dry contrast, to ~12 km (NLDAS-2 carries orographic precip/temperature variation across this high-relief basin)
Snow storage / melt contrast between years (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT, SNOW are in default output)

not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing — it cannot produce integrated streamflow at a gauge; needs an aggregation/routing step the stack lacks

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km elevation structure and ridgetop peak SWE
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 (0.125 deg) has no within-cell lapse rate; high ridgetop snow is averaged over terrain and underestimated
SNOTEL is sparse/missing in-domain, so the year-to-year SWE contrast cannot be checked against observations

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation x dominant soil), temporal contrast applied per column
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands span the rain-snow transition that dominates the wet/dry partitioning difference; x 2 dominant soil classes to separate texture control on infiltration/runoff from the climate signal = 8 columns. Each is run for BOTH 1993 and 2002, so the wet/dry contrast adds no columns. Smallest set that resolves both stratification axes.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate at the 2100-2700 m rain-snow transition (largest wet-vs-dry divergence in snow vs rain partitioning) and at valley bottoms where drainage/recharge storage response is strongest; downstream expander samples DEM + SSURGO to realize the band x soil cells.
sampling_strategy.replication: None beyond the soil crossing; heterogeneity is captured by strata rather than replicates to keep NLDAS cost (~10x Qian) defensible.

sampling_plan.reason: Captures largest snow-storage and melt-timing difference between wet 1993 and dry 2002 at the basin top.
Isolates the elevation band where wet/dry partitioning between snow and rain-driven runoff diverges most.
Mid-elevation, mostly rain-fed; tests how soil texture governs runoff vs infiltration under contrasting years.
ET-dominated, high evaporative demand; shows drought-year ET limitation and recharge shutoff.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — would require summing/routing column runoff (QOVER+QDRAI) to the gauge; NOT natively supported, so flagged as a gap rather than performed
validation_design.metric: bias / correlation (only if routing capability is added)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on gauge count; not usable without routing

validation_design.comparison: analog — could compare snow behavior to regional SNOTEL analog stations, clearly labelled as analog, not co-located
validation_design.metric: qualitative process check on melt timing / peak SWE ordering (1993 > 2002)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up; each column run for both 1993 (wet) and 2002 (dry)

requires_capabilities.why: convert independent-column runoff to integrated streamflow
resolve sub-12 km precip/temperature and ridgetop snow
requires_capabilities.blocks: fine elevation structure and accurate high-elevation SWE

requires_capabilities.why: initialize water table/storage so drainage-recharge contrast is not a cold-start artifact

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM elevation sampling + SSURGO soil raster + HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: expand band x soil strata into concrete points

assumptions: 1993 is representative wet and 2002 representative dry for this basin (user-specified; not independently verified here)
The basin lies within CONUS NLDAS-2 coverage so orographic forcing variation is available
Two dominant soil classes adequately represent SSURGO texture heterogeneity; expander will confirm actual dominant classes per band
Water-partitioning contrast is the primary deliverable; streamflow validation is deferred pending routing
open_questions: Are the two named years the intended wet/dry endpoints, or should they be selected from a precipitation percentile analysis of 1980-2018?
How many spin-up years are acceptable given NLDAS cost (~30 min/simulated year/column)?
Which specific USGS gauges are in-domain, and is adding a routing/aggregation step in scope for validation?
Is any regional SNOTEL analog acceptable for a labelled analog snow check?
